blockers: The completion validator does not validate completion of the pipeline. It ignores phase statuses and does not require build/static QA, browser QA, art QA, database update, or commit evidence; a third world can pass with a few files and an unrelated review.

Binding-review attribution is unsafe for third worlds: review runs are selected by substring matching the world name anywhere in task/artifact metadata, with no immutable pipeline-to-run reference or reviewed-artifact hash.
high: The gameplay-reference gate is global rather than world-specific: any existing entry in gameplay-references.json satisfies validation for a new third world.
Presentation QA is optional in validate-pipeline.mjs: omitting presentation_qa from pipeline.json skips the supposedly mandatory Asset Presentation Gate entirely.

present-shots.mjs remains substantially zoo-specific. It always executes four zoo bots before its generic walker, while the generic path captures only opening/area/first-game screens and does not verify failure, retry, success, JobReveal, or wrapUp for a third world.

Delegation observability is incomplete and fail-open: routing-log writes deliberately suppress all errors, and art-provider Codex generation calls are not logged. The sampled routing log also does not substantiate the pipelines' claimed review/delegation counts.

pipeline.json metrics remain manually aggregated self-attestations. validate-pipeline.mjs neither recomputes nor verifies delegation, repair, art-generation, QA-check, browser-flow, or human-intervention counts.
medium: The generic presentation walker silently tolerates missing first-Q1 and start controls: failure to find them produces no failure record, allowing misleadingly incomplete screenshot runs.
Completion validation checks only that gameplay-qa-<world>.mjs exists; it does not execute it or require a machine-readable successful result, so a placeholder or stale script qualifies.

Presentation validation accepts one PASS audit whose filename starts with the world name, regardless of required screen/viewport coverage, and also treats the shared town-map audit as evidence for every world.
The documented pipeline says browser QA covers entry through failure, retry, success, JobReveal, and wrapUp, but the reusable presentation walker does not enforce that contract for arbitrary worlds.
stages.json retains stale architecture language saying GATE 1/GATE 2 are the only human stops, while /new-world now describes autonomous default operation and additional HUMAN_REQUIRED conditions.
low: Art-loop and art-QA correctly enforce the new Series Style and Asset Presentation thresholds mechanically, but threshold/category definitions are duplicated between style-contract.md, prompts, and JavaScript, creating drift risk.
Provider freshness is enforced by art-loop.mjs but not by direct art-provider.mjs generation, leaving the adapter's safety claims dependent on callers using the intended wrapper.

recommended_actions: Replace validate-pipeline.mjs with a phase-schema validator requiring every mandatory phase to be present and done, with typed evidence records rather than prose.
Store explicit run IDs, reviewed artifact paths, and cryptographic hashes in pipeline.json; validate the exact final review against the current implementation hash.
Require target-world gameplay-reference entries for every designed Q1 and validate all required traceability fields.
Make presentation QA unconditional and require a manifest of expected screens for both viewports, including failure, retry, success, JobReveal, and wrapUp.
Move zoo deep-flow logic out of present-shots.mjs into a registered per-world bot and make the shared runner discover and execute the target world's bot.
Make routing-log writes mandatory or record a secondary durable failure; add logging around art-provider generation and assign invocation IDs shared across pipeline, run, and routing records.
Generate pipeline metrics mechanically from invocation/run/artifact records and reject human_interventions=0 when evidence is incomplete.
Require machine-readable successful outputs from build, static QA, gameplay QA, browser QA, art QA, and database validation—not merely scripts or prose claims.
Centralize all art thresholds and required categories in one machine-readable policy consumed by documentation, prompts, and enforcement code.
Update stages.json to match the current autonomous-default and HUMAN_REQUIRED architecture.
